title: Geolocation Capacity & Failover Request Orchestration (enterprise intake)
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: This ticket defines a lightweight, repeatable orchestration for intake and triage of enterprise requests relating to region availability and data residency. It covers three common customer asks: (1) add a new geography/region to Redwood hosted inference, (2) certify data residency for contract/sovereignty requirements, and (3) add regional failover paths for multi-region HA. Goal: reduce decision latency, produce consistent costing and SLA guidance, and identify mandatory legal/security gating criteria before onboarding work begins.

Scope: non-bug customer requests from Sales/CS/Customer Engineers. Not in scope: ad-hoc provider-specific provisioning work (handled by infra runbooks), one-off legal exceptions without follow-up roadmap.

Intake form (required fields):
- Customer name & account ID
- Primary contact and technical lead
- Specific request type: NEW_REGION | RESIDENCY_CERT | FAILOVER_PATH
- Requested earliest go-live date
- Data classification (public/internal/regulated/PHI/PII)
- Required SLA/throughput targets (qps, p50/p95 latency)
- Expected RPS and token profile (tokens/request, concurrent sessions)
- Regulatory constraints (country laws, audit requirements)
- Contract term implications (term length, penalties)
- Willingness to sign a residency addendum (yes/no)

Triage rubric (scoring, 0-10 each):
- Strategic fit (does this unlock > $X M ARR or a marquee customer): 0-10
- Technical complexity (new infra, cross-cloud, provider limitations): 0-10 (higher is harder)
- Operational cost delta (estimated annual additional infra/ops cost): 0-10
- Time-to-live impact (how quickly can we reasonably deliver): 0-10 (higher = longer)
- Compliance risk (legal/regulatory gating): 0-10

Decision thresholds (sum of weighted scores):
- Green (>=35): proceed to architecture & costed plan; assign Eng PRD and timeline.
- Amber (20-34): schedule scoping call with customer & legal; require executive approval for exceptions.
- Red (<20): deprioritize or offer alternate fallbacks (partner region, encrypted transit/caching).

Required attachments before engineering work:
- Legal template checklist (data transfer appendix, residency addendum)
- Initial cost estimate spreadsheet (hours + infra + marketplace fees)
- Proposed failover topology diagram (if failover request)
- Test plan for data locality and failover exercises

Operational playbooks created by this ticket:
1) New-region readiness checklist (networking, peering, images, infra templates, metrics)
2) Residency compliance playbook (KMS/HSM location, log routing, audit proof points)
3) Failover validation runbook (synthetic traffic, chaos tests, SLA verification)

Acceptance criteria:
- PM & Eng sign-off on triage decision within 10 business days of intake
- Cost + SLA proposal communicated to customer within 15 business days for Green items
- Legal approves residency language or documents an exception path

Risk & trade-offs:
- Adding regions increases operational overhead and long-tail costs; include amortized cost in prioritization.
- Strict on-prem/residency requirements may require Private deployments (higher revenue but longer lead time).
- Some cloud providers limit certain SKUs; fallback compatibility must be validated early.

Suggested owner roles:
- PM (request owner): triage, customer communications, prioritization
- Eng (solution owner): feasibility, cost estimate, rollout plan
- Legal: residency contract language and regulatory sign-off
- Security/Compliance: KMS placement, encryption validation, audit scope
- Solutions/SE: customer scoping and acceptance testing

Output artifacts for each intake (stored in shared Drive):
- triage-decision.yaml (summary metadata + score)
- costed-plan.xlsx
- low-level-arch.drawio
- runbook/residency-<customer>.md

Next steps for Green items:
1) Create ENG ticket(s) for infra provisioning and model image validation (link to ENG-IDs in Dependencies).
2) Schedule cross-functional kickoff (PM, Eng, Legal, Security, Solutions).
3) Commit targeted delivery milestone (MVP region gating, then full SLA enablement).
